work: Book of Hours, use of Clermont (Auvergne), France, 15th century. Clermont-Ferrand, Bibliothèque du Patrimoine (Clermont Auvergne Métropole), MS 2262, f. 12r: Hours of the Virgin, Matins, Psalm 8 (Domine Dominus noster).
note: "diplomatic" is what the scribe wrote, as read from this image (not yet checked against a facsimile edition): ſ = long s, s = round final s, ꝛ = r rotunda (after bowed letters), ꝓ = pro (p with a loop through the descender), ꝙ = quod, ꝫ = -m (the z-shaped final), macrons as written; [ ] = editorial expansion of a sign too small to show, [Q] etc. = painted initial. "edition" is the Vulgate text of Psalm 8 split at the manuscript's line breaks (the manuscript has "et opera" and "memores"). The scribe writes super/per in full: textura p bites into the following e, which can look like an abbreviation at small size. Line 21: the -us of dominus is a ligature, the round s fused to the second stroke of the u as its flag (after 'do' the ink holds exactly eight upright strokes: m, i, n and the u); the s is bracketed because it is not written as a letter of its own.
